claims.statement: Terminal, Metrics, Agent/SFTP and forwarding own separate SSH lifetimes. Terminal preparation/control exec and borrowed SFTP reuse its transport. Integration-enabled connect selects prepared startup: helpers are probed/installed through exec before PTY startup; optional install failure disables integration rather than typing a bootstrap, while a supplied launch can provide its own command. Ordinary PTY close retains transport only for live SFTP, not pending exec closes; prepared startup and supplied launches can separately retain control ownership. Retained-control PTY EOF completes CLOSE/FREE and releases its lease before reporting exit. SFTP drivers retain the worker without an owner-to-driver cycle; worker deinit cleans on its serial queue without reentrant synchronization. Saved intent does not restore live connections or prompts.

Port forwarding rules are saved descriptions rather than live listeners: they support local, remote, and dynamic kinds; dynamic rules clear target fields; validity requires a nonblank bind host and port 1 through 65535, plus a target host and port for non-dynamic rules.

Each physical SSH connection has a FIFO session budget shared by PTY, exec and SFTP, not forwarded TCP, listeners or jump bridges. Live ceiling updates do not revoke active leases; cancellation and budget close cancel queued admission. Runtime control exec uses non-queueing tryAcquire, refusing capacity when full or waiters exist. A one-slot ceiling makes published multiplexer context unavailable and removes ordinary-context draft read/replace capabilities.

Interactive SSH setup encodes configured environment variables with the connection charset and sends environment requests on the PTY after its PTY request and before shell or exec-based PTY startup. Individual server denials are nonfatal and report variable names; other errors fail startup. These requests are not inherited by preparation exec or non-PTY services.

ServerMetricsModel runs one serial worker per selected host. It connects a sampler with its own challenge-capable trust and keyboard-interactive handlers, publishes base samples before optional detail probes, and retries failed cycles with exponential delay capped at 60 seconds.

SSHMetricsSampler uses exclusive bounded SSH exec calls and marker framing to isolate structured metrics from remote shell preamble/trailer; malformed, truncated, or oversized output fails, while exit code 42 means unsupported primary metrics and GPU exit codes 42 or 6 mean no GPU.

PortForwardingController starts only valid SSH-enabled rules, shares a host-scoped forwarding context among active rules, computes its effective maximum from Host and app limits, and can update that maximum on a live context; per-rule generations reject stale callbacks and stopping the final rule retires the context.

A forwarding pool fans out only local and dynamic rules: it has one pool-level local listener per rule, registers those rules on healthy slots, assigns accepted flows to a least-loaded eligible slot with round-robin tie breaking, and keeps remote rules on the primary connection.

Forwarding auxiliary connections are filled with no more than four concurrent opens, install existing shared rules before publication, retry transient loss at 1/2/5/10/30-second delays, and do not automatically retry failures requiring interaction, trust, credentials, or cancellation.

Forwarding recovery and auxiliary opens forbid interaction and retain only reusable identity/route references rather than temporary passwords, passphrases, or once-only trust; existing TCP streams are not migrated or replayed after worker loss.

SFTP logical-file admission precedes context channel acquisition, so a global/per-host permit can be held while waiting for a per-connection session-channel lease. The scheduler no longer adds obsolete borrowed-resource exclusivity.

Desktop AppModel owns one ServerMetricsModel across windows, while iOS MobileMetricsModel wraps that same shared core implementation rather than implementing an independent sampler or authentication loop; both wire platform-specific sampler factories and Pro-dependent card limits into the core.

ServerMetricsModel persists ordered MetricsSelection intent, not monitor runtime; missing Hosts remain selected until available, SSH-disabled Hosts cannot be added, and a failed preference save leaves the in-memory configuration unchanged.

Metrics details register observers only while visible outside the connection journey, which gates filesystem/process probes in the shared worker; reading MetricsSnapshot does not admit Hosts or start collection and reports paused, sleeping, stopped and awaiting-authentication states.

A metrics monitor stops automatic retry when authentication needs attention or primary metrics are unsupported; sleep, disablement, shutdown, and changed Host connection configuration invalidate work and reset or retire the appropriate per-host sampler and interaction state.

Both macOS and iOS compose AgentKit built-ins, Termind host tools, and configured MCP tools through AssistantToolRegistry for tool-capable models; the app supplies Host, Agent connection/authentication/background, and metrics dependencies instead of borrowing terminal or forwarding service instances.

The Agent tool catalog composes runtime and app-owned executable definitions with stable presenter IDs for restored cards, using a closed legacy tool-name fallback only when a persisted descriptor has no presenter ID.

For tool-capable conversations AssistantToolRegistry creates a conversation-keyed scratch workspace reused across runs, emits plan presentations through the ordered Agent event channel, and configures only ssh_exec as a secret-consuming tool; its one-shot secret handles supply command stdin rather than SSH login.

Agent get_metrics resolves an SSH-capable Host and reads a cached MetricsSnapshotReading snapshot without connecting or triggering sampling; optional sections and five-minute trend report cached data that can be missing or stale.

Agent ssh_exec uses Agent authentication and a Host-keyed pooled SSH connection for non-PTY exec, with safe-command parallelism determined by risk preflight; libssh2 access is serialized by the worker and exec channels acquire the connection session budget.

Agent SSH authentication shares temporary credentials only among overlapping Host attempts, deleting its context with the last lease; its connection pool independently retains multiplexed Host connections across calls and runs until idle retirement or route change, and exclusive Agent SFTP work can choose silent auxiliary connections or primary sibling channels.

AssistantToolRegistry assembles executable tools only for models with tool-call ability, joining AgentKit built-ins, Termind host tools and configured MCP servers with AI-settings bearer credentials; it injects app-owned AgentHostServices components and the metrics reader rather than constructing their transports at registry creation.

AgentConnectionPool coalesces concurrent cold opens by Host and route fingerprint and disconnects a stale pooled connection on route change; exec retries exactly once when a connection was unavailable before channel opening, never replaying a command that started or a server-rejected channel.

Enabling a Host's SSH agent forwarding changes Agent exec ownership: the Agent pool opens separate per-call connections rather than caching a Host transport, closes them on exec-lease completion, and the authentication registry does not share its temporary Host authentication context in this mode; the ordinary pooled exec path and Metrics sampler disable SSH agent forwarding.

VaultSSHAgent grants agent forwarding as a per-physical-connection capability only when the Host and request permit it; revocation invalidates signing, keys are resolved at use rather than cached across connections, and signatures needing presence or an unsaved passphrase require an interactive policy.

The macOS app uses host-configured forwarding pooling with a Pro-dependent effective connection cap of one without multi-connection access, and updates existing contexts when that access changes; the host-configured factory constructs a pool even for target one, while iOS keeps a single-connection policy.

Group-bound Tailnet dialers never fall back to system networking on failure; managed Hosts cannot be jump Hosts. MultiConnectionPolicy resolves runtime fallback without changing saved SFTP or forwarding preferences.
